stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher quality model outputs, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first design, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating with popular local LLM runners.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, optimizing local AI inference.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, indicating active development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is connecting messaging workflows directly to local, private AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ford’s $30,000 electric truck: all the news about the company’s big EV re-do
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Ford is pivoting its EV strategy after the F-150 Lightning did not meet market expectations.
The automaker is developing a new Universal Electric Vehicle Platform for future models.
The first vehicle from this new platform is slated to be a $30,000 electric truck.

stories.title: Adobe’s ‘natural look’ camera app embraces generative AI
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Adobe's experimental camera app, Project Indigo, is integrating generative AI features.
The update aims to enhance the app's goal of providing a 'natural (SLR-like) look' for iPhone photography.
Notably, the AI tools being added do not rely on Adobe's proprietary Firefly AI models.

stories.title: Electric air taxis go to war
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Archer Aviation is expanding its electric aviation focus beyond commercial air taxis.
The company has co-developed a new aircraft with defense technology firm Anduril.
The new platform is designed with dual-use capabilities for both military and commercial applications.

stories.title: AliExpress fined almost $630 million over illegal product sales
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: AliExpress was fined approximately $629 million by the European Commission.
The fine stems from violations of the European Union's Digital Services Act (DSA).
The core violation was the platform's failure to effectively prevent the sale of illegal, unsafe, or counterfeit goods.

stories.title: AliExpress hit with record $625M fine after failing to make EU-ordered fixes
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: AliExpress received a record $625 million fine from EU regulators.
The fine stems from the retailer's failure to implement mandated fixes under the Digital Services Act (DSA).
The incident highlights increasing regulatory scrutiny and enforcement actions against major online platforms in the EU.

stories.title: Pay up or not? Ransomware surge has victims facing tough choices.
stories.author: Hannah Murphy, Financial Times
bullet_points: Ransomware attacks are increasing in sophistication, posing severe risks to victims.
Governments are actively considering legislation to prohibit the payment of ransoms.
The situation forces organizations and individuals into difficult strategic choices regarding threat response.

stories.title: India's first privately developed rocket reaches orbit on dramatic debut launch
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: India successfully launched its first privately developed rocket into orbit.
The launch was described as a dramatic debut, marking a significant milestone for private space ventures in India.
The achievement signals growing domestic capability and investment in the aerospace sector.

stories.title: Google-backed satellites for wildfire detection launch as smoke chokes US, Canada
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Google-backed FireSat program is launching satellites specifically designed for wildfire detection.
The new system claims the ability to detect wildfires that existing satellite technology overlooks.
The deployment is timely, addressing current severe wildfire smoke issues in the US and Canada.

stories.title: CRAFT: Clustering Rubrics to Diagnose Weak LLM Capabilities and Generate Targeted Fine-Tuning Data
stories.author: Yunzhong He
bullet_points: Introduces CRAFT, a new method to move beyond simple LLM performance measurement.
CRAFT converts rubric-based evaluation datasets into specific diagnoses of underlying LLM capability failures.
The goal is to generate targeted fine-tuning data to guide the next iteration of model improvement.

stories.title: Harmonizing AI Safety Thresholds
stories.author: Markov Grey
bullet_points: Frontier AI companies use disparate capability thresholds, hindering third-party verification and cross-company comparison.
Lack of common minimum safety thresholds risks inconsistent risk mitigation and a 'race to the bottom' in AI safety.
The paper proposes a methodology to derive harmonized safety thresholds across critical risk domains, including misuse (cyber and biological).

stories.title: PagedWeight: Efficient MoE LLM Serving with Dynamic Quality-Aware Weight Quantization
stories.author: Sasa Misailovic
bullet_points: Introduces PagedWeight, a novel serving method specifically designed for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs.
Addresses the critical tension between high GPU memory usage of MoE weights and growing KV cache demands during inference.
Achieves efficiency by dynamically quantizing MoE model weights at runtime, balancing weight precision against cache size.

stories.title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
stories.author: Oleg Ruchayskiy
bullet_points: Introduces ShellFlow, a novel Riemannian conditional flow matching model.
The model uses a single transformer to learn the structure of the Standard Model from LHC data.
It successfully spans a massive invariant mass range (sub-GeV to TeV) that is unachievable with standard Monte Carlo simulations.

stories.title: Frontier AI performance across the business disciplines: a case-grounded benchmark of knowledge work and analytical reasoning
stories.author: Mitch Weiss
bullet_points: Current LLM benchmarks fail to adequately measure AI performance in complex, real-world knowledge work.
The research focuses on benchmarking LLMs against tasks typical of white-collar professionals, such as synthesis and judgment.
This work highlights a critical gap in AI evaluation: moving beyond factual recall and coding to assess analytical reasoning.

stories.title: 7 Sandbox Escape Vulnerabilities Across 4 Coding Agent Vendors
stories.author: pillar.security by afogel
bullet_points: Seven sandbox escape vulnerabilities have been discovered across four different coding agent vendors.
This highlights critical security flaws within AI coding assistants, posing significant risks to users and systems.
The news is highly relevant to the rapidly growing field of AI development and software security.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon users with broader model access.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of 'subagents' for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added to Claude Code via Ollama integration.

stories.title: LG’s monitors come with an unwanted addition for Windows: McAfee pop-up ads
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: LG monitors are silently installing software via Windows Update upon first connection.
The installation includes the LG Monitor App Installer, which lacks visible user controls.
The issue raises concerns about unsolicited software installation and privacy on new hardware.

stories.title: Beyond grep: The case for a context-rich AI coding harness
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: The article discusses the need for 'context-rich AI coding harnesses' beyond simple tools like grep.
It features Vinay Perneti of Augment Code, focusing on the intersection of large language models and software development tooling.
The core theme is improving AI assistance in coding by providing deeper contextual understanding to the models.

stories.title: Will AI fix prior authorization—or make it worse?
stories.author: Joshua Cohen, Undark Magazine
bullet_points: Government is piloting an AI program to automate insurance coverage decisions.
The article explores the potential dual impact of AI on prior authorization processes.
The core question is whether AI will streamline or complicate existing healthcare administrative hurdles.

stories.title: Evaluating Open-Weight LLMs for Generating Structured Threat Information for Autonomous Vehicle Vulnerabilities
stories.author: Md Rayhanur Rahman
bullet_points: The research focuses on using Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) to process cybersecurity data.
The goal is to transform unstructured vulnerability data (like CVEs) into structured information relevant for Autonomous Vehicle (AV) security.
This addresses the critical need for security practitioners to analyze complex vulnerabilities across CAV components (sensors, ECUs, etc.).

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the Muon optimizer in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training, contrasting it with AdamW.
Applying Muon specifically to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework significantly boosted validation success (0.290 to 0.546).
The findings suggest Muon offers a tangible performance advantage in sparse-reward agentic RL tasks, unlike high-rate AdamW controls.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) perform 'active observation,' mirroring human vision.
Active observation is defined as a continuous, hypothesis-driven process of gaze redirection, rather than single-snapshot processing.
The authors introduce 'ActiveVision,' a new benchmark designed to empirically measure active observation capabilities in ML models.

stories.title: When Do Multi-Agent Systems Help? An Information Bottleneck Perspective
stories.author: Shuiwang Ji
bullet_points: The paper investigates when Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) outperform Single-Agent Systems (SAS) in complex tasks.
It utilizes an Information Bottleneck perspective to analyze the functional differences between MAS and SAS.
A key finding is that SAS maintains a full reasoning trace in a shared context, whereas MAS uses isolated local contexts connected by bounds.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses limitations in current methods, specifically struggling with locating visual evidence and interpreting structured scientific visuals.
Employs a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to integrate multimodal observations for reliable reasoning.

stories.title: A Methodology for Auditable Trustworthiness Levels in AI Lifecycle Governance
stories.author: Andrea Ferrario
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for ongoing, auditable trustworthiness assessment in AI systems throughout their lifecycle.
Identifies a gap where current AI trustworthiness research is either too abstract for monitoring or too narrow for governance needs.
Proposes a lightweight methodology designed to provide transparent and contestable documentation of AI trustworthiness levels.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in understanding the relationship between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It highlights two open research questions: how pretraining choices affect RL compute returns, and what specific changes RL induces in the model.
The study aims to overcome the difficulty of analyzing these interactions due to the vast and uncontrolled nature of pretraining corpora.

stories.title: Physics-enhanced reinforcement learning for real-time optimal control of dynamical systems
stories.author: Andrea Manzoni
bullet_points: The research addresses the sample inefficiency and high data requirements of standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) for complex control systems.
It proposes using physics-enhanced RL to improve the efficiency of synthesizing optimal control strategies for dynamical systems.
This work aims to overcome limitations in applying RL to high-dimensional spaces, which currently restricts its use to systems with sparse sensors/actuators.

stories.title: When Does Muon Help Agentic Reinforcement Learning?
stories.author: Hao Sun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the utility of the optimization algorithm 'Muon' specifically within agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training.
When applied to hidden weight matrices within the Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (GiGPO) framework, Muon significantly improved validation success from 0.290 to 0.546.
The findings suggest Muon offers a substantial performance advantage over high-rate AdamW controls in this specific RL context.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit 'active observation,' a key feature of human vision.
Active observation, where gaze is continuously redirected by hypotheses, is posited as essential for complex tasks, drawing from cognitive science.
The authors introduce ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed specifically to make the concept of active observation measurable for machine learning models.

stories.title: PRISA: Proactive Infrastructure LiDAR Framework for Intersection Safety Assessment
stories.author: Hoang H. Nguyen
bullet_points: Introduces PRISA, a new LiDAR framework designed for proactive safety assessment at urban intersections.
Focuses on real-time, continuous monitoring to anticipate traffic conflicts involving vehicles and vulnerable road users (VRUs).
Employs privacy-preserving and low-light-robust roadside sensors for long-term traffic observation.

stories.title: An Exam for Active Observers
stories.author: Willie Neiswanger
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in current benchmarks regarding whether Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit 'active observation,' a key concept from cognitive science.
Active observation posits that human vision is a continuous, hypothesis-driven process rather than a single snapshot.
The authors introduce ActiveVision, a new benchmark designed to empirically measure the presence of active observation in ML models.

stories.title: ToolSciVer: Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification with Visual Tool Augmented Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Rui Zhang
bullet_points: Introduces ToolSciVer, a novel framework for Multimodal Scientific Claim Verification (MSCV).
Addresses limitations in current methods by integrating visual evidence (figures, tables, charts) with textual context.
Utilizes a tool-augmented Reinforcement Learning approach to improve the location and interpretation of decisive visual evidence in scientific papers.

stories.title: Rate-Utility Frontiers for Language Encodings: Comparing Tokens, Bytes, and Pixels Under Controlled Linguistic Content
stories.author: Desmond Elliott
bullet_points: The research compares three different text encoding methods (tokens, bytes, and pixels) for language models.
The study controls for linguistic content and downstream model capacity to provide a fair comparison.
It utilizes parallel sentences across thirteen languages and five scripts to evaluate encoding preservation.

stories.title: Understanding Reasoning from Pretraining to Post-Training
stories.author: Pavel Izmailov
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between LLM pretraining and subsequent Reinforcement Learning (RL) fine-tuning.
It highlights two open research questions: how pretraining choices influence RL returns, and the specific impact of RL on the model.
The difficulty in studying this relationship stems from the vast and uncontrolled nature of pretraining corpora.

stories.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
stories.author: Kaifeng Lyu
bullet_points: Frontier Large Language Models (LLMs) exhibit surprising failures in basic tasks, specifically exact string copying.
The research attributes this failure to the inductive bias of positional encodings in Transformer architectures.
The models favor shortcut copying based on local context matching over precise positional recall.

stories.title: Loop the Loopies!
stories.author: Bryan Dai
bullet_points: Introduces 'Loopie,' a new family of powerful looped Transformer models.
The models utilize a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture, featuring sizes like 20B and 6B parameters.
Addresses a known limitation in looped Transformers regarding the scaling efficiency of increased pre-training compute.

stories.title: Nativ: Run frontier open models locally on your Mac
stories.author: aratahikaru5
bullet_points: Nativ allows users to run frontier open-source AI models locally on macOS.
This addresses the growing demand for local, private AI inference.
It lowers the barrier to entry for running powerful LLMs without cloud dependency.

stories.title: AI And Code Ownership: Who Is Responsible For Generated Code?
stories.author: nazar-boyko
bullet_points: The article addresses the complex legal question of code ownership when AI generates software.
It highlights the ambiguity surrounding intellectual property rights for AI-assisted code.
This topic signals an emerging legal and ethical challenge in the rapidly evolving field of AI development.

stories.title: Your AI Re-Reads Your Whole Codebase Every Session. Hand It a Map Instead
stories.author: lovestaco
bullet_points: Introduction of 'git-lrc,' a new Micro AI code reviewer.
The tool is designed to run on every code commit.
It aims to improve code review efficiency by providing context (a 'map') instead of re-scanning the entire codebase each time.
